It cuts both ways and the report should have said so: it further guts arm 5's justification, AND at 112 px tower pitch a single shape dropped between two towers is inside 100 px of BOTH and merges them into one component.

size_grade: DISAGREE — understated. 'Standard (10-30K)' is right for Lever A alone if the owner has already answered RULING 1. As scoped (three levers, one branch, 'any subset ships') it is Full (>30K), and the report's own reasoning gives the tier away when it says the four-option measured ruling package 'is most of the work'. Concretely, what pushes it over: (a) at least five test assertions go red that the report does not name — blueprintLegality.test.ts:163 for Lever A, :148-161 for the EDGE_PAD item, :266-273 ×3 for Lever C — and each needs re-deriving from the constant rather than re-pinning to a literal; (b) Lever B's target, footerBand.test.ts:383-413, pins the opaque-fill count at exactly 5 with 'IF THIS GOES RED, DO NOT BUMP THE NUMBER', and moving the cards off the band takes it to 4, so that guard must be honestly re-derived in a direction its own instruction does not anticipate; (c) the chord/merge/unrepairability mitigation is a real design decision touching dragPreview + placePrimitive + auto-bond, not a footnote; (d) the file set is ~14 files larger than stated. Per the project's own tier table this is a Full PDR — 3-way Council, 2 rounds, quality gate — not a 1-round Standard. And per CLAUDE.md's parallel-split lesson 5, the honest move is to split it: Lever A as its own branch with 'fix ONLY this, do not refactor', Lever B separately (it is render/input-only and carries zero hash risk), Lever C not at all until someone wants it.
net_assessment: A strong report with a soft middle. Its spine is sound and I could not break it: arm 5 at blueprintLegality.ts:194-200 really is the dead-space generator, the geometry is right to within 1 % on every number I could re-derive by hand (62,356 px² removed per turret against my 63,108 upper bound; 31,784 against 32,179; 148 → 112 spacing; the 64 px bottom band), and the two most load-bearing structural claims — that no legality predicate reads the art, and that the bottom menu is UI-layer click swallowing rather than geometry — are both CONFIRMED against the source. The measurement discipline is real, not prose. Where it fails is the S182 pattern exactly: it fixed what was asked and left defects behind it. Three classes. (1) TESTS IT DID NOT RUN THE NUMBERS ON. At least five assertions go red that tests_owed does not contain, including the one test in the whole repo written to pin the very behaviour Lever A changes (blueprintLegality.test.ts:163). It also asserts a protective binding that does not exist (blueprints.test.ts:172 is a literal 60), and it calls the EDGE_PAD change 'free and safe … the branch can still ship it with no ruling' when that change alone reds a five-recipe `it.each` and falsifies a live safety docblock at placeFromFree.ts:275-277. A branch handed this brief would ship believing it had cover it does not have. (2) IT CLEARED A DETERMINISM HAZARD IT DID NOT LOOK FOR.
